case_title.reason: Matches the judgment's caption: Markash Jajara v. The State of Assam & Anr.

number_of_accused.reason: Single appellant whose liability is decided.

accused_gender.reason: Accused is referred to as the appellant, the victim's father-in-law's counterpart, and as 'he'; male is supported.

accused_age.reason: No age of the accused is stated.

accused_religion.reason: No religion is stated or described.

accused_caste.reason: No caste, tribe or community is named.

accused_occupation.reason: No occupation of the accused is mentioned.

accused_socioeconomic_status.quote: owing to his poor financial conditions, the appellant's appeal was forwarded by the Jail Authorities
accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Judgment expressly describes the accused's poor financial condition.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record is mentioned.

victim_gender.quote: his younger brother – Markush Borja had been assaulted and killed
victim_gender.reason: Victim is male (the deceased, a brother and husband).

victim_caste.reason: No caste or community of the victim is named.

victim_religion.reason: No religion of the victim is stated.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: murder of his son-in-law, namely, late Markush Borja
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Relationship as son-in-law (relative) is accurately described.

offence_category.quote: the act of the appellant in causing injuries to the deceased falls within the expression of `culpable homicide' which does not amount to `murder'
offence_category.reason: Charged as murder, but the Court held the final offence is culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

statutory_provisions.reason: s.302 IPC is the charged section; Exception I of s.300 is correctly noted as considered.

weapon.quote: assaulted and killed by the appellant with a bamboo stick
weapon.reason: Bamboo stick, also described as bamboo lathi, is supported.

evidence_type.reason: Extra-judicial confession, PW-6 testimony, medical, circumstantial and non-eyewitness evidence are all present in the judgment.

confession.quote: the Supreme Court read PW-6's evidence in its entirety
confession.reason: Oral confession to daughter and PW-1's account are described; Court accepted causing of injuries.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Fatal head injury per autopsy surgeon; no other aggravating facts noted by the Court
aggravating_circumstances.quote: the injury sustained over the head by the deceased is fatal to cause instantaneous death
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Third laceration is 'just below the chin', not on the head as stated.

mitigating_circumstances.quote: suddenly thrashed his son-in-law with the bamboo stick
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Provocation, loss of self-control, no premeditation and protective motive are supported.

trial_court_outcome.correct_value: Guilty under s.302 IPC; life imprisonment and fine of Rs.10,000 (six months imprisonment in default)
trial_court_outcome.quote: sentenced to undergo life imprisonment with a fine of Rs.10,000/- with the stipulated imprisonment of six months on default
trial_court_outcome.reason: The judgment does not describe the default imprisonment as simple.

high_court_outcome.quote: The Gauhati High Court has dismissed the jail appeal
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court dismissed the appeal, upholding conviction and sentence.

final_outcome.quote: the act of the appellant ... falls within the expression of `culpable homicide'
final_outcome.reason: Conviction altered to a lesser offence and sentence changed, matching conviction_modified.

offence_finally_established.quote: falls within the expression of `culpable homicide' which does not amount to `murder'
offence_finally_established.reason: Final offence is culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

imprisonment_type.reason: Final sentence is a fixed term of rigorous imprisonment.

imprisonment_years.reason: Ten years is the final fixed term.

fine_rs.quote: The sentence as awarded by the courts below stands modified accordingly
fine_rs.reason: Court only modified imprisonment; the Rs.10,000 fine from courts below was not expressly altered.

neutral_facts.reason: Neutral summary uses no names or outcomes and covers incident and evidence without revealing the verdict.

offence_severity.reason: The judgment does not state the statutory maximum or minimum for s.302.

attempt_completion.quote: the deceased suffered the following injuries
attempt_completion.reason: Death was caused, so the offence is completed.

physical_harm.quote: the injury sustained over the head by the deceased is fatal to cause instantaneous death
physical_harm.reason: Death from head lacerations and fatal injury is supported.

number_of_offences.correct_value: 1 charged; 0 finally upheld under s.302 (conviction altered to culpable homicide not amounting to murder)
number_of_offences.quote: sentence of life imprisonment awarded to the appellant to rigorous imprisonment of ten years
number_of_offences.reason: s.302 conviction was not upheld; the final conviction is for a different offence.

financial_property_loss.reason: No money or property loss is involved.

premeditation_planning.quote: the appellant did not have any pre-meditated intention to commit the murder of his son-in-law
premeditation_planning.reason: Court expressly found no pre-meditated intention.

motive.quote: The appellant's motive at best was to prevent the deceased from misbehaving with his daughter after consuming alcohol
motive.reason: Motive accepted by the Court is accurately stated.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: The appellant and the deceased were the only ones present in the house at the time of occurrence
key_evidence_accepted.reason: PW-6 testimony, presence-only evidence and post-mortem findings were relied on.

witness_credibility.quote: the statement of P.W.6 - Sarani Boria needs to be appreciated in its entirety
witness_credibility.reason: Court's assessment of PW-6 and the non-eyewitness status of PW-8 is accurately reported.

post_offence_conduct.quote: My father was also taken to the police station.
post_offence_conduct.reason: Confession to daughter and taking to police station are supported by the testimony.

trial_duration.quote: judgment and order dated 03.10.2016, passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Jorhat
trial_duration.reason: Trial judgment, High Court and Supreme Court dates match the judgment.

legal_representation.quote: Gaurav Agrawal, Adv. for the Appellant. Nalin Kohli, Sr. AAG
legal_representation.reason: Counsel for appellant and State are correctly listed.

investigation_status.quote: FIR, under Section 302 IPC, was registered on the receipt of an ejahar submitted by P.W.8
investigation_status.reason: FIR, arrest, chargesheet, nine witnesses and completed trial are supported.

procedural_irregularity.reason: No procedural lapse is noted by the Court.

appeal_history.reason: Outcomes at trial court, High Court and Supreme Court are accurately described.

prosecution_argument.reason: The judgment records no State arguments in the Supreme Court.

defence_argument.quote: the defence did not question the two witnesses on the same
defence_argument.reason: Records no Supreme Court defence arguments and accurately reports High Court defence contentions.

legal_principle_applied.quote: whilst deprived of the power of self-control by grave and sudden provocation
legal_principle_applied.reason: Exception I to s.300 with provocation analysis is the applied principle.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Ajay Sing -Vs- State of Maharashtra reported in (2007) 12 sec 341
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Precedent was cited by the High Court, not the Supreme Court, as the value states.

sentencing_rationale.correct_value: Ends of justice would be adequately met by converting life imprisonment to rigorous imprisonment of ten years
sentencing_rationale.quote: the ends of justice would be adequately met by converting the sentence of life imprisonment
sentencing_rationale.reason: Court gave ends-of-justice rationale; linking it expressly to provocation and no premeditation is inference.

judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: The fatal occurrence was seemingly the final culmination of loss of the power of self-control
judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Provocation, loss of self-control, no premeditation and protective motive are weighed by the Court.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The Court weighed no aggravating factors.

other_sentence_order.quote: The appellant shall be released on completion of the requisite and reduced period of sentence
other_sentence_order.reason: Release order and disposal of interlocutory applications are accurately noted.
